meta.dataset: world-atlas 2.0.2 countries-50m (Natural Earth 1:50m) + Natural Earth 1:10m reconstruction units
meta.notes: Modern source units are only geometry blocks. The authored 1900 transfers in boundaries_1900.json are applied with polygon-clipping; every polity carries boundary provenance, a reference date, a geometry class and a confidence class. Internal modern borders are not drawn. South Africa uses the four 1900 polities with modern province proxies; the Transvaal and Orange Free State are documented approximations.

boundarySources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Germany' and 'Prussia'
boundarySources.notes: Contemporary description of the German Empire's constituent states and its eastern provinces, including Posen, West Prussia, East Prussia and Silesia.

boundarySources.notes: Contemporary description of Ottoman Tripolitania, the vilayet of Tripoli, the sanjak of Benghazi and the Fezzan; used for the Libyan provincial components and the note on limited effective control in the interior.

boundarySources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Darfur'
boundarySources.notes: Describes the restored Darfur Sultanate after 1898 and its approximate western Sudanese extent; used for the reconstructed Darfur polygon.

boundarySources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Wadai'

boundarySources.title: Hammond's Modern Atlas of the World (1912)
boundarySources.notes: Political atlas contemporary with the reference date; cross-check for European, African and Asian external borders.

boundarySources.title: The Times Survey Atlas of the World (1920), historical political sheets

boundarySources.title: Karte Deutsches Reich, Verwaltungsgliederung 1900-01-01 (Wikimedia Commons)
boundarySources.notes: Administrative map of the German Empire on the reference date; used to check Alsace-Lorraine, the Prussian eastern provinces, Schleswig-Holstein and the constituent states.

boundarySources.title: Reichsgesetzblatt 1871, Treaty of Frankfurt boundary annexations
boundarySources.notes: Primary instrument transferring Alsace and the Moselle departments to the German Empire.

boundarySources.title: Treaty of Versailles (1919), territorial clauses
boundarySources.notes: Used inversely to identify what the German Empire held in 1900: Alsace-Lorraine, Posen, West Prussia, parts of Silesia, Memel, northern Schleswig and Eupen-Malmedy.

boundarySources.title: Treaty of Saint-Germain (1919), Austro-Hungarian territorial clauses
boundarySources.notes: Used inversely for Galicia, Bukovina, Transylvania, Vojvodina, South Tyrol, Trieste and the Dalmatian coast.

boundarySources.title: Treaty of Trianon (1920), Hungarian territorial clauses
boundarySources.notes: Used inversely for the Hungarian half of Austria-Hungary, including Transylvania, Slovakia, Vojvodina and Kotor.

boundarySources.title: Treaty of Lausanne (1923), Ottoman successor boundaries
boundarySources.notes: Used inversely for Ottoman Europe and Anatolia: Kars/Ardahan/Artvin to Russia in 1878, Crete autonomous, and the Balkan/Macedonian provinces still Ottoman in 1900.

boundarySources.title: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium Agreement (1899)
boundarySources.notes: Defines the Sudan condominium that in 1900 still excluded Darfur.

boundarySources.title: British Aden and the Aden Protectorate, 1839-1900
boundarySources.notes: Aden and its hinterland were British Indian territory in 1900; the Ottoman-Yemeni frontier was not delimited until 1904-1914, so the southern limit is approximate.

boundarySources.title: historical-basemaps world_1900 (cross-check only)
boundarySources.notes: Used only as a visual and topological cross-check for the German eastern border and the broad extent of the Ottoman Sahara. No coordinate ring from this dataset is redistributed; all final geometry is rebuilt from public-domain modern units and the explicit transfer polygons above.

boundarySources.title: CShapes 2.0 (classification reference only)
boundarySources.notes: Consulted for status coding only; not used for geometry.

boundarySources.title: Century M11c authored boundary reconstruction
boundarySources.notes: Explicit transfer polygons, clipping lines and per-polity provenance. Every reconstructed frontier is labelled HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; approximate lines are not presented as exact.
